title: CAQH Index Report 2024: eligibility and benefit verification, dental sections

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: CAQH (nonprofit health-care industry alliance; data collection with NORC at the University of Chicago)
source_type: Industry benchmarking survey report (voluntary survey of plans and providers)
reliability: Industry-alliance survey report; voluntary participation, data reflect calendar year 2023. CAQH promotes electronic transactions, so its savings framing carries that interest. The ADA and NDEDIC encouraged members to contribute data.
findings: For 2023, the dental industry conducted an estimated 1.2 billion eligibility and benefit verifications, up 24 percent; verifications were 24 percent of total dental transaction volume.

Dental spending on eligibility and benefit verification rose 15 percent to $2.1 billion, the largest increase among dental administrative tasks measured and 30 percent of total dental administrative spend.

CAQH attributes the dental increase to higher volume and higher cost of conducting a check via a plan portal, "the highest portal cost among the dental transactions"; it states variations in portal requirements and formats add complexity.

CAQH estimates the dental savings opportunity from switching to fully electronic (270/271) checks at $580 million (up seven percent), and an average time savings opportunity of 8 minutes per transaction for dental providers (12 minutes for medical).

A dental practice quoted in the report: "When it comes to eligibility and benefits, I don't have an automated tool that I can trust, so I don't use it." The report says dental providers report that automated responses often lack robust enough dental-specific information to trust.

CAQH cost per transaction counts only labor (salaries, wages, benefits, overhead) for conducting the transaction, not information gathering or follow-up, and excludes system costs. Data collected by voluntary online survey July to September 2024.
limitations: Findings read from pdftotext output of the report; the bar-chart values for dental adoption and volume by mode were garbled in extraction and are not recorded.
Industry-wide dental figures; no breakdown by practice size, so small-practice burden is not isolated.
Voluntary survey with honoraria for providers; representativeness is weighted by CAQH but was not independently assessed.
The report cites a 12 percent claim denial rate for 2023 sourced to an Optum index that is not dental-specific; not used here.
Cost figures are modeled labor cost per transaction, not measured staff hours in a given practice. Dated: 2023 data, report published 2024.
Exact publication date not shown in the document text read (report year 2024 / December 2025 inferred).
